content.value: Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language known for its readability and large ecosystem of libraries.

concepts.name: Python
concepts.description: A high-level programming language known for readable syntax and broad use in scripting, automation, data work, and applications.

concepts.name: Interpreter
concepts.description: A program that executes code directly by reading and running instructions rather than producing a separate compiled binary first.

concepts.name: Script
concepts.description: A file of code intended to be run as a program or automation task.

concepts.name: Expression
concepts.description: Code that evaluates to a value, such as a calculation, variable reference, or function call.

concepts.name: Statement
concepts.description: A complete instruction in a program, such as an assignment, conditional, loop, or function call.

concepts.name: Standard library
concepts.description: The collection of modules included with Python that provide common functionality without extra installation.

content.value: You can run Python code using the interactive interpreter, scripts executed from the command line, or environments such as Jupyter notebooks and IDEs.

concepts.name: Python REPL
concepts.description: An interactive Python session where code is entered and evaluated one statement or expression at a time.

concepts.name: Script execution
concepts.description: Running a saved program file so the interpreter executes its statements in order.

concepts.name: Terminal command
concepts.description: A text command entered in a shell to run programs, navigate files, or perform development tasks.

concepts.name: Syntax error
concepts.description: An error caused by code that violates the grammar rules of the programming language.

concepts.name: Runtime error
concepts.description: An error that occurs while a program is executing, even if the code syntax is valid.

concepts.name: Program output
concepts.description: Text, values, files, or behavior produced by a program when it runs.

content.value: Python variables are created when you assign a value using =. Python uses dynamic typing, so you do not need to declare types explicitly.

concepts.name: Variable
concepts.description: A name that refers to a value stored or computed by a program.

concepts.name: Assignment
concepts.description: The act of binding a value to a variable name.

concepts.name: String
concepts.description: A sequence of text characters stored as a value.

concepts.name: Integer
concepts.description: A whole-number value without a fractional part.

concepts.name: Float
concepts.description: A numeric value that can represent decimal or fractional quantities.

concepts.name: Boolean
concepts.description: A true-or-false value used in logic and control flow.

concepts.name: Type conversion
concepts.description: Changing a value from one data type to another, such as from text to a number.

content.value: The print() function outputs text, and input() reads a line of user input as a string.

concepts.name: print()
concepts.description: A Python function that writes text or values to the console output.

concepts.name: input()
concepts.description: A Python function that reads text entered by the user from the console.

concepts.name: Prompt
concepts.description: Text shown to a user to ask for input or guide an action.

concepts.name: String interpolation
concepts.description: Inserting variable values or expressions into a string to produce formatted text.

concepts.name: User input
concepts.description: Data provided by a person while a program is running.

concepts.name: Console output
concepts.description: Text or values displayed in the terminal or command-line interface.

content.value: If statements allow you to execute code only when a condition is true. You can also use elif and else for multiple branches.

concepts.name: Conditional statement
concepts.description: A control-flow structure that chooses which code runs based on a condition.

concepts.name: if
concepts.description: The keyword that starts a conditional branch when a condition is true.

concepts.name: elif
concepts.description: A Python keyword for checking an additional condition after a previous if condition was false.

concepts.name: else
concepts.description: The branch that runs when earlier conditions in a conditional statement are false.

concepts.name: Boolean expression
concepts.description: An expression that evaluates to true or false.

concepts.name: Code block
concepts.description: A grouped set of statements that belong to a control structure such as a conditional or loop.

content.value: Python supports for loops for iterating over sequences and while loops for running code while a condition remains true.

concepts.name: for loop
concepts.description: A loop that repeats once for each item in a sequence or iterable.

concepts.name: while loop
concepts.description: A loop that repeats as long as its condition remains true.

concepts.name: Iteration
concepts.description: One repetition of a loop or the process of stepping through items one at a time.

concepts.name: Sequence traversal
concepts.description: Visiting each item in an ordered collection such as a string, list, or range.

concepts.name: Loop condition
concepts.description: The expression that controls whether a loop continues running.

concepts.name: Infinite loop
concepts.description: A loop that never reaches a stopping condition and continues indefinitely.

questions.question: Which loop is best for iterating over each item in a list?
options: for loop directly over the list

content.value: Python uses logical operators such as and, or, and not to combine or invert boolean expressions.

concepts.name: and
concepts.description: A logical operator that is true only when both connected conditions are true.

concepts.name: or
concepts.description: A logical operator that is true when at least one connected condition is true.

concepts.name: not
concepts.description: A logical operator that reverses the truth value of a condition.

concepts.name: Comparison operator
concepts.description: An operator such as ==, !=, <, or > that compares values and returns a Boolean result.

concepts.name: Truth value
concepts.description: Whether a value or expression is treated as true or false in a Boolean context.

concepts.name: Compound condition
concepts.description: A condition made by combining multiple Boolean expressions with logical operators.

content.value: Combining variables, input, if statements, and loops allows you to build simple interactive scripts, such as guessing games or basic calculators.

concepts.name: Program flow
concepts.description: The order in which a program’s statements execute.

concepts.name: Pseudocode
concepts.description: Plain-language or code-like planning text used to design program logic before writing exact syntax.

concepts.name: Input-process-output
concepts.description: A basic program pattern where data is received, transformed, and then displayed or returned.

concepts.name: Variable update
concepts.description: Changing the value associated with a variable during program execution.

concepts.name: Branch tracing
concepts.description: Following conditional logic step by step to determine which branch runs.

concepts.name: Loop tracing
concepts.description: Following a loop step by step to track iterations, conditions, and variable changes.
